text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A provincial senator of the opposition Zambia Democratic Congress says the party is under pressure, from an Islamic group which funded its campaign in last year's elections, to unseat the government through violence.
- Deputy health minister Nkandu Luo says about 4,000 Zambians die of AIDS every year.
- The United Transport and Taxis Association says new bus fares resulting from a 24 percent rise in fuel prices will come into effect on Tuesday.
- Former president Kenneth Kaunda could face treason charges following government allegations that he is training mercenaries to destabilise the country.
